etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: First attested in 1567; borrowed from Latin obviātus, perfect passive participle of obviō (“to block, to hinder”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).
senses: (transitive) To make (something) unnecessary; to anticipate and prevent or bypass (something which would otherwise have been necessary or required)
(transitive) To avoid (a future problem or difficult situation).

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: Borrowed from Latin obviātus, see Etymology 1, -ate (noun-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix).
